name: Sow Thistle

facts.how: Raw when young, cooked when older

caution: Soft spineless leaves and milky sap; a harmless dandelion relative. Harvest away from sprayed ground. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Looks thistly but the soft edges don't bite. Break a stem and it bleeds white, like its cousin the dandelion.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Young leaves are mild and juicy in salad; older ones lose their slight bitterness with a quick cooking.
